claim: Salicylate inhibits CBP acetyltransferase activity in vitro with an IC50 of 5.7 mM.
source: Salicylate effectively inhibited p300 dependent acetyltransferase activity (IC50 = 10.2 mM) and CBP-mediated acetyltransferase activity (IC50 = 5.7 mM) in vitro
evidence: The IC50 value is directly measured from in vitro acetyltransferase assays with recombinant CBP and histones.

claim: Salicylate inhibits p300 acetyltransferase activity in vitro with an IC50 of 10.2 mM.
source: Salicylate effectively inhibited p300 dependent acetyltransferase activity (IC50 = 10.2 mM) and CBP-mediated acetyltransferase activity (IC50 = 5.7 mM) in vitro
evidence: The IC50 value is directly measured from in vitro acetyltransferase assays with recombinant p300 and histones.

claim: Salicylate does not detectably inhibit PCAF acetyltransferase in vitro.
source: Salicylate effectively inhibited p300 dependent acetyltransferase activity (IC50 = 10.2 mM) and CBP-mediated acetyltransferase activity (IC50 = 5.7 mM) in vitro, but did not detectably inhibit PCAF or GCN5 acetyltransferases (Figure 1A) in vitro.
evidence: Figure 1A shows that PCAF activity remains at ~100% across all salicylate concentrations tested.

claim: Salicylate does not detectably inhibit GCN5 acetyltransferase in vitro.
source: Salicylate effectively inhibited p300 dependent acetyltransferase activity (IC50 = 10.2 mM) and CBP-mediated acetyltransferase activity (IC50 = 5.7 mM) in vitro, but did not detectably inhibit PCAF or GCN5 acetyltransferases (Figure 1A) in vitro.
evidence: Figure 1A shows that GCN5 activity remains at ~100% across all salicylate concentrations tested.

claim: Salicylate binds to the p300 HAT domain.
source: To confirm that salicylate binds to p300, we used thermal stability assays.
evidence: Thermal stability assays show that salicylate reduces the thermal unfolding temperature of p300 in a dose-dependent manner.

claim: Treatment with 10 mM salicylate reduces the thermal unfolding temperature of p300/acetyl-CoA from 48.6°C to 46.1°C.
source: This experiment revealed that the thermal unfolding temperature of p300/acetyl-CoA was 48.6°C, while treatment with 10 and 25 mM salicylate reduced the unfolding temperature to 46.1°C and 40.8°C, respectively (Figure 1B).
evidence: Thermal melt curves in Figure 1B directly show the shift in melting temperature upon salicylate treatment.

claim: Treatment with 25 mM salicylate reduces the thermal unfolding temperature of p300/acetyl-CoA from 48.6°C to 40.8°C.
source: This experiment revealed that the thermal unfolding temperature of p300/acetyl-CoA was 48.6°C, while treatment with 10 and 25 mM salicylate reduced the unfolding temperature to 46.1°C and 40.8°C, respectively (Figure 1B).
evidence: Thermal melt curves in Figure 1B directly show the shift in melting temperature upon salicylate treatment.

claim: Salicylate exhibits direct competitive inhibition of p300 against acetyl-CoA.
source: Kinetic analysis of p300 acetyltransferase activity with various concentrations of acetyl-CoA (Figure 1C) and histone (Figure 1D) substrates revealed that salicylate exhibits direct competitive p300 inhibition against acetyl-CoA and noncompetitive inhibition against histones.
evidence: Lineweaver-Burk plot in Figure 1C shows intersecting lines at the y-axis, characteristic of competitive inhibition.

claim: Salicylate exhibits noncompetitive inhibition of p300 against histones.
source: Kinetic analysis of p300 acetyltransferase activity with various concentrations of acetyl-CoA (Figure 1C) and histone (Figure 1D) substrates revealed that salicylate exhibits direct competitive p300 inhibition against acetyl-CoA and noncompetitive inhibition against histones.
evidence: Lineweaver-Burk plot in Figure 1D shows a pattern consistent with noncompetitive inhibition.

claim: Salicylate inhibits p300 acetyltransferase activity by directly competing with acetyl-CoA binding near its binding site on CBP and p300.
source: Taking this data together, we surmised that salicylate inhibits p300 acetyltransferase activity by directly competing with acetyl-CoA binding near its binding site on CBP and p300.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the combination of thermal stability assays showing binding and kinetic analysis showing competitive inhibition with acetyl-CoA.

claim: Salicylate treatment induces deacetylation of H2AK5/K9 in HEK293T cells in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Western blot analysis with antibodies against various specific acetyl-lysine modifications of histone H2A, H2B, H3, and H4 showed that addition of salicylate correlated with the deacetylation of H2AK5/K9, H2BK12/K15, and H3K56 in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Figure 2A shows dose-dependent decrease in H2AK5 and H2AK9 acetylation with increasing salicylate concentrations.

claim: Salicylate treatment induces deacetylation of H2BK12/K15 in HEK293T cells in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Western blot analysis with antibodies against various specific acetyl-lysine modifications of histone H2A, H2B, H3, and H4 showed that addition of salicylate correlated with the deacetylation of H2AK5/K9, H2BK12/K15, and H3K56 in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Figure 2A shows dose-dependent decrease in H2BK12/K15 acetylation with increasing salicylate concentrations.

claim: Salicylate treatment induces deacetylation of H3K56 in HEK293T cells in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Western blot analysis with antibodies against various specific acetyl-lysine modifications of histone H2A, H2B, H3, and H4 showed that addition of salicylate correlated with the deacetylation of H2AK5/K9, H2BK12/K15, and H3K56 in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Figure 2A shows dose-dependent decrease in H3K56 acetylation with increasing salicylate concentrations.

claim: The IC50 for salicylate-mediated inhibition of H2B acetylation is 4.8 mM.
source: The IC50 for salicylate-mediated inhibition of H2B acetylation (4.8 mM) was close to the IC50 of CBP measured in vitro and to the plasma concentrations of salicylate (1–3 mM) in humans after oral administration (Goldfine et al., 2010; 2013).
evidence: The IC50 value is derived from dose-response curves in Figure 2A showing H2B acetylation levels at different salicylate concentrations.

claim: Plasma concentrations of salicylate in humans after oral administration range from 1-3 mM.
source: The IC50 for salicylate-mediated inhibition of H2B acetylation (4.8 mM) was close to the IC50 of CBP measured in vitro and to the plasma concentrations of salicylate (1–3 mM) in humans after oral administration (Goldfine et al., 2010; 2013).
evidence: This information is supported by citations to Goldfine et al., 2010 and 2013.

claim: Salicylate treatment does not change the acetylation state of H3K9, K14, K27, K36 and H4K5, K8, K12, K16.
source: Other histone residues, including H3K9, K14, K27, K36 and H4K5, K8, K12, K16, have also been reported to be acetylated by CBP/p300 (Schiltz et al., 1999; Kouzarides, 2007), but their acetylation state did not change in response to salicylate
evidence: Figure 2A shows that these histone marks remain relatively unchanged across salicylate concentrations.

claim: H3K9, K14, K27, K36 and H4K5, K8, K12, K16 are acetylated by CBP/p300.
source: Other histone residues, including H3K9, K14, K27, K36 and H4K5, K8, K12, K16, have also been reported to be acetylated by CBP/p300 (Schiltz et al., 1999; Kouzarides, 2007)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schiltz et al., 1999 and Kouzarides, 2007.

claim: The lack of change in acetylation of some histone residues in response to salicylate is possibly due to redundant activity of other acetyltransferases in the cellular environment.
source: but their acetylation state did not change in response to salicylate, possibly as a consequence of redundant activity of other acetyltransferases in the cellular environment (Kouzarides, 2007) or opposing effects caused by inhibition of its previously characterized targets.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed data, supported by citation to Kouzarides, 2007.

claim: Overexpression of wild type p300 suppresses the effect of salicylate on H2BK12/K15 acetylation in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Overexpression of WT p300 suppressed the effect of salicylate in a dose-dependent manner and increased H2BK12/K15 acetylation (Figure 2B)
evidence: Figure 2B shows that increasing amounts of p300 plasmid transfection increase the IC50 of salicylate for H2B acetylation inhibition.

claim: Overexpression of catalytically inactive p300 mutants does not suppress the effect of salicylate on H2BK12/K15 acetylation.
source: but overexpression of catalytically inactive p300 mutants (Figure 2C) and PCAF did not (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Figure 2C shows that catalytically inactive p300 mutants (Y1503A and F1504A) do not rescue H2B acetylation in the presence of salicylate.

claim: Overexpression of PCAF does not suppress the effect of salicylate on H2BK12/K15 acetylation.
source: but overexpression of catalytically inactive p300 mutants (Figure 2C) and PCAF did not (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Figure 2D shows that PCAF overexpression does not rescue H2B acetylation in the presence of salicylate.

claim: The IC50 of salicylate strongly correlates with the amount of transfected p300.
source: Furthermore, the IC50 of salicylate strongly correlated with the amount of transfected p300 but not PCAF (Figure 2E).
evidence: Figure 2E shows a linear correlation (R²=0.99) between p300 plasmid amount and IC50 of salicylate.

claim: The IC50 of salicylate does not correlate with the amount of transfected PCAF.
source: Furthermore, the IC50 of salicylate strongly correlated with the amount of transfected p300 but not PCAF (Figure 2E).
evidence: Figure 2E shows no correlation (R²=0.09) between PCAF plasmid amount and IC50 of salicylate.

claim: Salicylate-mediated H2B deacetylation is specifically due to inhibition of p300 acetyltransferase activity.
source: These findings support the hypothesis that salicylate-mediated H2B deacetylation is specifically due to inhibition of p300 acetyltransferase activity.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the rescue experiments showing that only wild-type p300, but not catalytically inactive mutants or PCAF, can rescue salicylate-induced deacetylation.

claim: Salicylate decreases acetylation of NF-κB p65K310 in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Salicylate decreased acetylation of both NF-κB and p53 in a dose-dependent manner.
evidence: Figure 2F shows dose-dependent decrease in NF-κB p65K310 acetylation with increasing salicylate concentrations.

claim: Salicylate decreases acetylation of p53K382 in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Salicylate decreased acetylation of both NF-κB and p53 in a dose-dependent manner.
evidence: Figure 2G shows dose-dependent decrease in p53K382 acetylation with increasing salicylate concentrations.

claim: p300 acetyltransferase activity is a biologically relevant target for salicylate in vivo in cultured cells.
source: These findings strongly support the hypothesis that p300 acetyltransferase activity is a biologically relevant target for salicylate in vivo in cultured cells.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the combined data showing salicylate inhibits p300 in vitro and reduces acetylation of both histone and non-histone proteins in cells.

claim: Salicylate activates AMPK.
source: Recently, salicylate was reported to activate AMPK by allosteric binding to its AMP binding site. (Hawley et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hawley et al., 2012.

claim: Salicylate treatment increases levels of phosphorylated ACC in HEK293T cells in a dose-dependent manner.
source: To confirm this finding, we treated HEK293T cells with various doses of salicylate. The levels of a phosphorylated form of acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC), an established AMPK target, increased in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2G).
evidence: Figure 2G shows dose-dependent increase in phosphorylated ACC with increasing salicylate concentrations.

claim: Compound C suppresses p-ACC accumulation in response to salicylate.
source: Compound C, an AMPK inhibitor, suppressed p-ACC accumulation in response to salicylate, but did not inhibit deacetylation of acetylated H2BK12/K15 or acetyl-p53K382.
evidence: Figure 2G shows that Compound C treatment reduces p-ACC levels in salicylate-treated cells.

claim: Compound C does not inhibit salicylate-induced deacetylation of H2BK12/K15.
source: Compound C, an AMPK inhibitor, suppressed p-ACC accumulation in response to salicylate, but did not inhibit deacetylation of acetylated H2BK12/K15 or acetyl-p53K382.
evidence: Figure 2G shows that H2BK12/K15 acetylation remains decreased in the presence of both salicylate and Compound C.

claim: Compound C does not inhibit salicylate-induced deacetylation of p53K382.
source: Compound C, an AMPK inhibitor, suppressed p-ACC accumulation in response to salicylate, but did not inhibit deacetylation of acetylated H2BK12/K15 or acetyl-p53K382.
evidence: Figure 2G shows that p53K382 acetylation remains decreased in the presence of both salicylate and Compound C.

claim: Salicylate-mediated protein deacetylation is not dependent on AMPK activation and activity.
source: This experiment demonstrates that salicylate-mediated protein deacetylation is not dependent on AMPK activation and activity (Figure 2G).
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the observation that AMPK inhibition by Compound C does not prevent salicylate-induced deacetylation.

claim: 4-aminosalicylic acid inhibits p300 with an IC50 of 12.4 mM.
source: We tested their ability to inhibit CBP/p300 acetyltransferase activity in in vitro HAT assays. All five drugs inhibited p300 with different IC50 (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: Figure 3A shows the IC50 value of 12.4 mM for 4-aminosalicylic acid.

claim: 5-aminosalicylic acid inhibits p300 with an IC50 of 76 mM.
source: We tested their ability to inhibit CBP/p300 acetyltransferase activity in in vitro HAT assays. All five drugs inhibited p300 with different IC50 (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: Figure 3A shows the IC50 value of 76 mM for 5-aminosalicylic acid.

claim: Diflunisal inhibits p300 with an IC50 of 996 μM.
source: Three of the drugs inhibited p300 more potently than salicylate: the antidiabetes drug repaglinide (IC50 = 374 μM), the immunosuppressant mycophenolic acid (IC50 = 664 μM), and diflunisal, an older nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (IC50 = 996 μM) (Figure 3, A and B).
evidence: Figure 3A shows the IC50 value of 996 μM for diflunisal.

claim: Mycophenolic acid inhibits p300 with an IC50 of 664 μM.
source: Three of the drugs inhibited p300 more potently than salicylate: the antidiabetes drug repaglinide (IC50 = 374 μM), the immunosuppressant mycophenolic acid (IC50 = 664 μM), and diflunisal, an older nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (IC50 = 996 μM) (Figure 3, A and B).
evidence: Figure 3A shows the IC50 value of 664 μM for mycophenolic acid.

claim: Repaglinide inhibits p300 with an IC50 of 374 μM.
source: Three of the drugs inhibited p300 more potently than salicylate: the antidiabetes drug repaglinide (IC50 = 374 μM), the immunosuppressant mycophenolic acid (IC50 = 664 μM), and diflunisal, an older nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (IC50 = 996 μM) (Figure 3, A and B).
evidence: Figure 3A shows the IC50 value of 374 μM for repaglinide.

claim: Repaglinide inhibits p300 more potently than salicylate.
source: Three of the drugs inhibited p300 more potently than salicylate: the antidiabetes drug repaglinide (IC50 = 374 μM), the immunosuppressant mycophenolic acid (IC50 = 664 μM), and diflunisal, an older nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (IC50 = 996 μM) (Figure 3, A and B).
evidence: Comparison of IC50 values shows repaglinide (374 μM) is more potent than salicylate (10.2 mM).

claim: Mycophenolic acid inhibits p300 more potently than salicylate.
source: Three of the drugs inhibited p300 more potently than salicylate: the antidiabetes drug repaglinide (IC50 = 374 μM), the immunosuppressant mycophenolic acid (IC50 = 664 μM), and diflunisal, an older nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (IC50 = 996 μM) (Figure 3, A and B).
evidence: Comparison of IC50 values shows mycophenolic acid (664 μM) is more potent than salicylate (10.2 mM).

claim: Diflunisal inhibits p300 more potently than salicylate.
source: Three of the drugs inhibited p300 more potently than salicylate: the antidiabetes drug repaglinide (IC50 = 374 μM), the immunosuppressant mycophenolic acid (IC50 = 664 μM), and diflunisal, an older nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (IC50 = 996 μM) (Figure 3, A and B).
evidence: Comparison of IC50 values shows diflunisal (996 μM) is more potent than salicylate (10.2 mM).

claim: Repaglinide induces insulin secretion at nanomolar concentration.
source: Since repaglinide induces insulin secretion at nanomolar concentration, it is likely that its ability to inhibit p300 with an IC50 of 374 μM is irrelevant to its antidiabetic activity.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about repaglinide's mechanism of action.

claim: Repaglinide's ability to inhibit p300 with an IC50 of 374 μM is likely irrelevant to its antidiabetic activity.
source: Since repaglinide induces insulin secretion at nanomolar concentration, it is likely that its ability to inhibit p300 with an IC50 of 374 μM is irrelevant to its antidiabetic activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the large difference between the nanomolar concentration needed for insulin secretion and the 374 μM IC50 for p300 inhibition.

claim: Diflunisal induces deacetylation of H2AK5 in HEK293T cells.
source: Diflunisal induced deacetylation of specific histone residues, H2AK5, K9, H2BK12/K15, H3K56 (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1)
evidence: Figure 3C shows dose-dependent decrease in H2AK5 acetylation with increasing diflunisal concentrations.

claim: Diflunisal induces deacetylation of H2AK9 in HEK293T cells.
source: Diflunisal induced deacetylation of specific histone residues, H2AK5, K9, H2BK12/K15, H3K56 (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1)
evidence: Figure 3C shows dose-dependent decrease in H2AK9 acetylation with increasing diflunisal concentrations.

claim: Diflunisal induces deacetylation of H2BK12/K15 in HEK293T cells.
source: Diflunisal induced deacetylation of specific histone residues, H2AK5, K9, H2BK12/K15, H3K56 (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1)
evidence: Figure 3C shows dose-dependent decrease in H2BK12/K15 acetylation with increasing diflunisal concentrations.

claim: Diflunisal induces deacetylation of H3K56 in HEK293T cells.
source: Diflunisal induced deacetylation of specific histone residues, H2AK5, K9, H2BK12/K15, H3K56 (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1)
evidence: Figure 3C shows dose-dependent decrease in H3K56 acetylation with increasing diflunisal concentrations.

claim: Diflunisal induces a pattern of histone acetylation similar to that induced by salicylate.
source: Diflunisal induced deacetylation of specific histone residues, H2AK5, K9, H2BK12/K15, H3K56 (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1), a pattern of histone acetylation similar to that induced by salicylate.
evidence: Comparison of Figure 2A and Figure 3C shows similar patterns of histone deacetylation for both drugs.

claim: The IC50 for diflunisal inhibition of H2BK12/K15 in cells is 160 μM.
source: Importantly, the IC50 for H2BK12/K15 inhibition in cells was 160 μM, which is within the range of plasma concentrations of diflunisal (150–350 μM) after daily oral administration (Nuernberg et al., 1991; Mano et al., 2006).
evidence: This IC50 value is derived from dose-response curves in Figure 3C.

claim: Plasma concentrations of diflunisal after daily oral administration range from 150-350 μM.
source: Importantly, the IC50 for H2BK12/K15 inhibition in cells was 160 μM, which is within the range of plasma concentrations of diflunisal (150–350 μM) after daily oral administration (Nuernberg et al., 1991; Mano et al., 2006).
evidence: This information is supported by citations to Nuernberg et al., 1991 and Mano et al., 2006.

claim: Overexpression of wild type p300 suppresses the effect of diflunisal on H2BK12/K15 acetylation in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Overexpression of WT p300 suppressed the effect of diflunisal in a dose-dependent manner and increased H2BK12/K15 acetylation (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 2)
evidence: Figure 3D shows that increasing amounts of p300 plasmid transfection increase H2B acetylation levels in the presence of diflunisal.

claim: Overexpression of catalytically inactive p300 mutants does not suppress the effect of diflunisal on H2BK12/K15 acetylation.
source: but overexpression of catalytically inactive p300 mutants did not (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Figure 3E shows that catalytically inactive p300 mutants (Y1503A and F1504A) do not rescue H2B acetylation in the presence of diflunisal.

claim: Diflunisal suppresses acetylation of NF-κB p65K310.
source: Diflunisal also suppressed acetylation of the nonhistone proteins NF-κB p65K310 (Figure 3F) and p53K382 (Figure 3G).
evidence: Figure 3F shows dose-dependent decrease in NF-κB p65K310 acetylation with increasing diflunisal concentrations.

claim: Diflunisal suppresses acetylation of p53K382.
source: Diflunisal also suppressed acetylation of the nonhistone proteins NF-κB p65K310 (Figure 3F) and p53K382 (Figure 3G).
evidence: Figure 3G shows dose-dependent decrease in p53K382 acetylation with increasing diflunisal concentrations.

claim: Compound C suppresses p-ACC accumulation in response to diflunisal.
source: Here also, Compound C, an AMPK inhibitor, suppressed p-ACC accumulation in response to diflunisal, but did not inhibit deacetylation of acetylated H2BK12/K15 or acetyl-p53K382
evidence: Figure 3G shows that Compound C treatment reduces p-ACC levels in diflunisal-treated cells.

claim: Compound C does not inhibit diflunisal-induced deacetylation of H2BK12/K15.
source: Here also, Compound C, an AMPK inhibitor, suppressed p-ACC accumulation in response to diflunisal, but did not inhibit deacetylation of acetylated H2BK12/K15 or acetyl-p53K382
evidence: Figure 3G shows that H2BK12/K15 acetylation remains decreased in the presence of both diflunisal and Compound C.

claim: Compound C does not inhibit diflunisal-induced deacetylation of p53K382.
source: Here also, Compound C, an AMPK inhibitor, suppressed p-ACC accumulation in response to diflunisal, but did not inhibit deacetylation of acetylated H2BK12/K15 or acetyl-p53K382
evidence: Figure 3G shows that p53K382 acetylation remains decreased in the presence of both diflunisal and Compound C.

claim: AMPK is not necessary for diflunisal-induced deacetylation effects.
source: indicating that AMPK is not necessary for these effects (Figure 3G).
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the observation that AMPK inhibition by Compound C does not prevent diflunisal-induced deacetylation.

claim: Diflunisal targets p300 acetyltransferase activity independently of AMPK.
source: These findings support the model that diflunisal also targets p300 acetyltransferase activity independently of AMPK.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the combined data showing diflunisal inhibits p300 and that AMPK inhibition does not prevent diflunisal's effects on acetylation.

claim: The leukemogenicity of the AML1-ETO fusion protein is regulated by p300-mediated acetylation of lysine 43 of the fusion protein.
source: Previously, we reported that the leukemogenicity of the AML1-ETO fusion protein, generated by a t(8;21) translocation in acute myelogenous leukemia, is regulated by p300-mediated acetylation of lysine 43 of the fusion protein (Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2011.

claim: Salicylate decreases K24 and K43 acetylation of AML1-ETO in Kasumi-1 cells in a dose-dependent manner.
source: In support of our model, K24 and K43 acetylation of AML1-ETO were decreased in a dose-dependent manner by salicylate (Figure 4A, left)
evidence: Figure 4A (left panel) shows dose-dependent decrease in AML1-ETO K24 and K43 acetylation with increasing salicylate concentrations.

claim: Diflunisal decreases K24 and K43 acetylation of AML1-ETO in Kasumi-1 cells in a dose-dependent manner.
source: In support of our model, K24 and K43 acetylation of AML1-ETO were decreased in a dose-dependent manner by salicylate (Figure 4A, left) and by diflunisal (Figure 4A, right).
evidence: Figure 4A (right panel) shows dose-dependent decrease in AML1-ETO K24 and K43 acetylation with increasing diflunisal concentrations.

claim: Salicylate inhibits Kasumi-1 cell proliferation at concentrations as low as 1 mM.
source: Salicylate inhibited cell proliferation at concentrations as low as 1 mM (Figure 4B).
evidence: Figure 4B shows reduced cell counts in Kasumi-1 cells treated with 1 mM salicylate compared to untreated controls.

claim: Salicylate-induced growth inhibition in Kasumi-1 cells is caused in part by increased apoptosis.
source: This growth inhibition was caused in part by increased apoptosis, as shown by annexin V/7AAD double staining (Figure 4C).
evidence: Figure 4C shows increased annexin V positive cells in salicylate-treated Kasumi-1 cells.

claim: Diflunisal increases apoptosis in Kasumi-1 and AE9a cells in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Diflunisal also increased apoptosis in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 4D).
evidence: Figure 4D shows dose-dependent increase in annexin V positive cells with increasing diflunisal concentrations.

claim: Salicylate causes a dose-dependent increase of the sub-G1 cell fraction in Kasumi-1 and AE9a cells.
source: Additional measurements of nuclear DNA distribution showed a dose-dependent increase of the sub-G1 cell fraction, highly suggestive of apoptotic fragmentation by salicylate (Figure 4E)
evidence: Figure 4E shows dose-dependent increase in sub-G1 fraction with increasing salicylate concentrations.

claim: Diflunisal causes a dose-dependent increase of the sub-G1 cell fraction in Kasumi-1 cells.
source: Additional measurements of nuclear DNA distribution showed a dose-dependent increase of the sub-G1 cell fraction, highly suggestive of apoptotic fragmentation by salicylate (Figure 4E) and diflunisal (Figure 4F).
evidence: Figure 4F shows dose-dependent increase in sub-G1 fraction with increasing diflunisal concentrations.

claim: Salicylate treatment increases the fraction of G1 cells in Kasumi-1 and AE9a cells.
source: We also noted an increased fraction of G1 cells and a decreased fraction of S and G2/M cells after salicylate treatment
evidence: This is stated as an observation from cell cycle analysis data.

claim: Salicylate treatment decreases the fraction of S and G2/M cells in Kasumi-1 and AE9a cells.
source: We also noted an increased fraction of G1 cells and a decreased fraction of S and G2/M cells after salicylate treatment
evidence: This is stated as an observation from cell cycle analysis data.

claim: CBP/p300 is required for the G1/S transition.
source: consistent with reports that CBP/p300 is required for the G1/S transition (data not shown) (Ait-Si-Ali et al., 2000; Iyer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ait-Si-Ali et al., 2000 and Iyer et al., 2007.

claim: Salicylate does not affect the surface expression of CD11b and CD34 in Kasumi-1 cells.
source: Salicylate did not affect the surface expression of differentiation-related antigens (CD11b and CD34 in Kasumi-1, Mac-1 and C-kit in AE9a) (data not shown)
evidence: This is stated as an observation from flow cytometry analysis.

claim: Salicylate does not affect the surface expression of Mac-1 and C-kit in AE9a cells.
source: Salicylate did not affect the surface expression of differentiation-related antigens (CD11b and CD34 in Kasumi-1, Mac-1 and C-kit in AE9a) (data not shown)
evidence: This is stated as an observation from flow cytometry analysis.

claim: Acetylation of AML1-ETO is required for self-renewal and leukemogenesis but not for its ability to block cell differentiation.
source: in accordance with our previous finding that acetylation of AML1-ETO is required for self-renewal and leukemogenesis but not for its ability to block cell differentiation (Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2011.

claim: Kasumi-1 cells transduced with empty vector show inhibition of growth by diflunisal.
source: Cells transduced with the empty vector showed inhibition of growth by diflunisal, similar to untransduced cells (Figure 4H).
evidence: Figure 4H shows reduced cell counts in empty vector-transduced Kasumi-1 cells treated with diflunisal.

claim: p300-transduced Kasumi-1 cells are significantly more resistant to diflunisal than empty vector-transduced cells.
source: In contrast, p300-transduced cells were significantly more resistant to diflunisal (Figure 4H and I)
evidence: Figure 4H and I show higher cell counts in p300-transduced Kasumi-1 cells treated with diflunisal compared to empty vector controls.

claim: p300-transduced Kasumi-1 cells exhibit less apoptosis than empty vector-transduced cells when treated with diflunisal.
source: and exhibit less apoptotis measured by annexin V positive cells (Figure 4J) and sub-G1 fraction (Figure 4K).
evidence: Figure 4J and K show lower percentages of annexin V positive cells and sub-G1 fraction in p300-transduced cells treated with diflunisal.

claim: Diflunisal kills Kasumi-1 cells by apoptosis due to p300 inhibition.
source: These results support the model that diflunisal kills Kasumi-1 cells by apoptosis due to p300 inhibition.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the rescue experiments showing that p300 overexpression protects Kasumi-1 cells from diflunisal-induced apoptosis.

claim: Diflunisal reduces tumor volumes in SCID mice inoculated with Kasumi-1 cells in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Diflunisal reduced tumor volumes in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 5A)
evidence: Figure 5A shows smaller tumor volumes in mice treated with 50 or 100 mg/kg diflunisal compared to vehicle controls.

claim: Diflunisal has minimal effects on body weight in SCID mice inoculated with Kasumi-1 cells.
source: Diflunisal reduced tumor volumes in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 5A) and had minimal effects on body weight (Figure 5B).
evidence: Figure 5B shows similar body weights across vehicle and diflunisal-treated groups.

claim: After 3 weeks of diflunisal treatment, tumors were significantly smaller in diflunisal-treated mice than in vehicle-treated controls.
source: After 3 weeks of treatment, the tumors were significantly smaller in diflunisal-treated mice than in vehicle-treated controls (Figure 5C)
evidence: Figure 5C shows smaller final tumor volumes in diflunisal-treated mice compared to vehicle controls.

claim: Most tumors disappeared in mice treated with 100 mg/kg diflunisal.
source: and most of the tumors had disappeared in mice treated with the higher dose of diflunisal (Figure 5D).
evidence: Figure 5C shows that most mice in the 100 mg/kg diflunisal group have tumor volumes near zero.

claim: Salicylate inhibits CBP and p300 lysine acetyltransferase activity in vitro by direct competition with acetyl-Coenzyme A at the catalytic site.
source: Here we show that salicylate specifically inhibits CBP and p300 lysine acetyltransferase activity in vitro by direct competition with acetyl-Coenzyme A at the catalytic site.
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the abstract, supported by kinetic analysis and thermal stability assays.

claim: At concentrations attainable in human plasma after oral administration, both salicylate and diflunisal blocked the acetylation of lysine residues on histone and non-histone proteins in cells.
source: At concentrations attainable in human plasma after oral administration, both salicylate and diflunisal blocked the acetylation of lysine residues on histone and non-histone proteins in cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by cellular acetylation data showing IC50 values within the range of plasma concentrations.

claim: Diflunisal suppressed the growth of p300-dependent leukemia cell lines expressing AML1-ETO fusion protein in vitro.
source: Finally, we found that diflunisal suppressed the growth of p300-dependent leukemia cell lines expressing AML1-ETO fusion protein in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by cell proliferation and apoptosis data in Kasumi-1 and AE9a cells.

claim: Diflunisal suppressed the growth of p300-dependent leukemia cell lines expressing AML1-ETO fusion protein in vivo.
source: Finally, we found that diflunisal suppressed the growth of p300-dependent leukemia cell lines expressing AML1-ETO fusion protein in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by xenograft data showing reduced tumor volumes in diflunisal-treated mice.

claim: Acetylsalicylic acid (Aspirin) inhibits prostaglandin biosynthesis by irreversibly inactivating cyclooxygenases via non-enzymatic acetylation of a single serine residue.
source: One of its widely used derivatives, acetylsalicylic acid (Aspirin), inhibits prostaglandin biosynthesis by irreversibly inactivating cyclooxygenases via non-enzymatic acetylation of a single serine residue (Warner et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Warner et al., 1999.

claim: Salicylic acid does not possess acetylating activity.
source: Interestingly, salicylic acid does not possess this acetylating activity (since it is lacking the acetyl group) and does not inhibit cyclooxygenase in vitro.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the structural difference between salicylic acid and aspirin.

claim: Salicylic acid does not inhibit cyclooxygenase in vitro.
source: Interestingly, salicylic acid does not possess this acetylating activity (since it is lacking the acetyl group) and does not inhibit cyclooxygenase in vitro.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about salicylic acid's lack of direct cyclooxygenase inhibition.

claim: Salicylic acid blocks cyclooxygenase expression at the transcriptional level.
source: However, salicylic acid blocks cyclooxygenase expression at the transcriptional level thereby explaining its anti-inflammatory properties (Xu et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Xu et al., 1999.

claim: Both salicylic acid and aspirin inhibit nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) activity.
source: In addition, both salicylic acid and aspirin inhibit nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) activity (Kopp and Ghosh, 1994) by inhibiting IκB kinase β (IKKβ) (Yin et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kopp and Ghosh, 1994 and Yin et al., 1998.

claim: Salicylic acid and aspirin inhibit IκB kinase β (IKKβ).
source: In addition, both salicylic acid and aspirin inhibit nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) activity (Kopp and Ghosh, 1994) by inhibiting IκB kinase β (IKKβ) (Yin et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yin et al., 1998.

claim: Salicylate inhibits the JNK pathway.
source: Other possible mechanisms of action have been proposed that include JNK pathway inhibition (Schwenger et al., 1997) and direct allosteric activation of AMP kinase (AMPK) (Hawley et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schwenger et al., 1997.

claim: Salicylate directly and allosterically activates AMP kinase (AMPK).
source: Other possible mechanisms of action have been proposed that include JNK pathway inhibition (Schwenger et al., 1997) and direct allosteric activation of AMP kinase (AMPK) (Hawley et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hawley et al., 2012.

claim: Salsalate is an effective therapy for type 2 diabetes.
source: Salsalate, a salicylate precursor, is an effective therapy for type 2 diabetes (Goldfine et al., 2010)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Goldfine et al., 2010.

claim: Type 2 diabetes is a metabolic disorder associated with insulin resistance and a strong pro-inflammatory component dependent on NF-κB.
source: Salsalate, a salicylate precursor, is an effective therapy for type 2 diabetes (Goldfine et al., 2010), a metabolic disorder associated with insulin resistance and a strong pro-inflammatory component dependent on NF-κB (Donath and Shoelson, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Donath and Shoelson, 2011.

claim: The efficacy of salicylates on insulin resistance is thought to reflect its anti-inflammatory activity and to be mediated by IKKβ inhibition.
source: The efficacy of salicylates on insulin resistance is thought to reflect its anti-inflammatory activity and to be mediated by IKKβ inhibition (Yin et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism supported by citation to Yin et al., 1998.

claim: Anacardic acid contains a salicylic acid moiety linked to a long alkyl chain.
source: Interestingly, examination of the chemical structure of anacardic acid, a previously reported p300 inhibitor, revealed that it contained a salicylic acid moiety linked to a long alkyl chain (Balasubramanyam et al., 2003; Sung et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Balasubramanyam et al., 2003 and Sung et al., 2008.

claim: Anacardic acid is a p300 inhibitor.
source: Interestingly, examination of the chemical structure of anacardic acid, a previously reported p300 inhibitor, revealed that it contained a salicylic acid moiety linked to a long alkyl chain (Balasubramanyam et al., 2003; Sung et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Balasubramanyam et al., 2003 and Sung et al., 2008.

claim: Full activation of NF-κB activity requires the reversible acetylation of NF-κB by CBP/p300 histone acetyltransferases (HATs).
source: Previously, we showed that full activation of NF-κB activity requires the reversible acetylation of NF-κB by CBP/p300 histone acetyltransferases (HATs) (Chen et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2001.

claim: Salicyl-CoA inhibits CBP/p300 with an IC50 of 220 μM.
source: Indeed, we have found that salicyl-CoA, a known major intermediate of salicylate metabolism (Knights et al., 2007), inhibits CBP/p300 with 28-fold increased potency in comparison with salicylate: IC50=220 μM for salicyl-CoA vs 6.12 mM for salicylate (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This IC50 value is measured from dose-response curves in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Salicyl-CoA inhibits CBP/p300 with 28-fold increased potency compared to salicylate.
source: Indeed, we have found that salicyl-CoA, a known major intermediate of salicylate metabolism (Knights et al., 2007), inhibits CBP/p300 with 28-fold increased potency in comparison with salicylate: IC50=220 μM for salicyl-CoA vs 6.12 mM for salicylate (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is calculated from the ratio of IC50 values: 6.12 mM / 220 μM ≈ 28-fold.

claim: Salicyl-CoA is a known major intermediate of salicylate metabolism.
source: Indeed, we have found that salicyl-CoA, a known major intermediate of salicylate metabolism (Knights et al., 2007), inhibits CBP/p300 with 28-fold increased potency in comparison with salicylate
evidence: This is supported by citation to Knights et al., 2007.

claim: Diflunisal-CoA inhibits CBP/p300 with an IC50 of 20 μM.
source: A similar 52-fold increase in potency is observed with diflunisal-CoA in comparison to diflunisal: IC50=20 μM for diflunisal-CoA vs 1.05 mM for diflunisal (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This IC50 value is measured from dose-response curves in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Diflunisal-CoA inhibits CBP/p300 with 52-fold increased potency compared to diflunisal.
source: A similar 52-fold increase in potency is observed with diflunisal-CoA in comparison to diflunisal: IC50=20 μM for diflunisal-CoA vs 1.05 mM for diflunisal (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is calculated from the ratio of IC50 values: 1.05 mM / 20 μM ≈ 52-fold.

claim: In plants, salicylate acts as an immune signal to induce systemic acquired resistance.
source: In plants, from where it was originally isolated, salicylate acts as an immune signal to induce systemic acquired resistance.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about salicylate's role in plant immunity.

claim: Salicylate specifically activates the transcription cofactor NPR1 by binding to its paralogs NPR3 and NPR4.
source: It specifically activates the transcription cofactor NPR1 (nonexpressor of PR genes 1) by binding to its paralogs NPR3 and NPR4 (Fu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Fu et al., 2012.

claim: Plants contain an ortholog of p300/CBP.
source: Since plants contain an ortholog of p300/CBP (Bordoli et al., 2001), some of its activities in plants could also be mediated by inhibition of the plant ortholog of p300 or CBP.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bordoli et al., 2001.

claim: Some of salicylate's activities in plants could be mediated by inhibition of the plant ortholog of p300 or CBP.
source: Since plants contain an ortholog of p300/CBP (Bordoli et al., 2001), some of its activities in plants could also be mediated by inhibition of the plant ortholog of p300 or CBP.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on the presence of p300/CBP orthologs in plants and the finding that salicylate inhibits mammalian p300/CBP.

claim: Many mechanisms of action have been proposed for the anti-inflammatory effects of salicylate in mammalian cells, including weak inhibition of cyclooxygenase.
source: Many mechanisms of action have been proposed for the anti-inflammatory effects of salicylate in mammalian cells, including weak inhibition of cyclooxygenase (Warner et al., 1999)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Warner et al., 1999.

claim: Many mechanisms of action have been proposed for the anti-inflammatory effects of salicylate in mammalian cells, including inhibition of IKKβ.
source: Many mechanisms of action have been proposed for the anti-inflammatory effects of salicylate in mammalian cells, including weak inhibition of cyclooxygenase (Warner et al., 1999), inhibition of IKKβ inhibition (Yin et al., 1998)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yin et al., 1998.

claim: Many mechanisms of action have been proposed for the anti-inflammatory effects of salicylate in mammalian cells, including inhibition of topoisomerase II.
source: Many mechanisms of action have been proposed for the anti-inflammatory effects of salicylate in mammalian cells, including weak inhibition of cyclooxygenase (Warner et al., 1999), inhibition of IKKβ inhibition (Yin et al., 1998) and topoisomerase II (Cox et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cox et al., 2011.

claim: Many mechanisms of action have been proposed for the anti-inflammatory effects of salicylate in mammalian cells, including modulation of NF-κB.
source: Many mechanisms of action have been proposed for the anti-inflammatory effects of salicylate in mammalian cells, including weak inhibition of cyclooxygenase (Warner et al., 1999), inhibition of IKKβ inhibition (Yin et al., 1998) and topoisomerase II (Cox et al., 2011), modulation of NF-κB (Kopp and Ghosh, 1994)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kopp and Ghosh, 1994.

claim: Many mechanisms of action have been proposed for the anti-inflammatory effects of salicylate in mammalian cells, including activation of AMPK.
source: Many mechanisms of action have been proposed for the anti-inflammatory effects of salicylate in mammalian cells, including weak inhibition of cyclooxygenase (Warner et al., 1999), inhibition of IKKβ inhibition (Yin et al., 1998) and topoisomerase II (Cox et al., 2011), modulation of NF-κB (Kopp and Ghosh, 1994), and activation of AMPK (Hawley et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hawley et al., 2012.

claim: The acetylation of both histones and non-histone proteins (NF-κB) is suppressed in cells treated with either salicylate or diflunisal.
source: We observed that the acetylation of both histones and non-histone proteins (NF-κB) is suppressed in cells treated with either salicylate or diflunisal.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Histone AcH3K56 is the most sensitive histone acetyl mark to inhibition by both salicylate and diflunisal.
source: We identified histone AcH3K56 as the most sensitive histone acetyl mark to inhibition by both drugs.
evidence: This is inferred from the dose-response curves in Figures 2A and 3C showing H3K56 has the steepest decline.

claim: CBP (also known as Nejire) in flies and CBP and p300 in humans acetylate H3K56.
source: This results is highly consistent with the literature showing that CBP (also known as Nejire) in flies and CBP and p300 in humans acetylate H3K56 (Das et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Das et al., 2009.

claim: The pattern of histone marks inhibition are remarkably similar between salicylate and diflunisal, but at different concentrations.
source: We also note that the pattern of histone marks inhibition are remarkably similar between the two drugs, but at different concentrations in agreement with their relative abilities to inhibit p300/CBP in vitro.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of Figures 2A and 3C showing similar patterns of histone deacetylation.

claim: Many histone modifications are regulated by multiple HAT enzymes.
source: Indeed, many histone modifications are regulated by multiple HAT enzymes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about histone acetylation.

claim: Acetyl H4K5 is regulated by HAT1, CBP, p300, Tip60, and HB01.
source: For example, acetyl H4K5 is regulated by HAT1, CBP, p300, Tip60, HB01 whereas acetyl H3 K14 is regulated by CBP, p300, PCAF, gcn5, ScSAS3 (Kouzarides, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kouzarides, 2007.

claim: Acetyl H3K14 is regulated by CBP, p300, PCAF, gcn5, and ScSAS3.
source: For example, acetyl H4K5 is regulated by HAT1, CBP, p300, Tip60, HB01 whereas acetyl H3 K14 is regulated by CBP, p300, PCAF, gcn5, ScSAS3 (Kouzarides, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kouzarides, 2007.

claim: The lack of inhibition of some histone H3 or H4 acetylation sites by salicylate or diflunisal reflects the compensating activities of other histone acetyltransferases that target the same sites.
source: We therefore interpret the observed lack of inhibition of some histone H3 or H4 acetylation sites by salicylate or diflunisal to reflect the compensating activities or other histone acetyltransferases that target the same sites.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data based on knowledge of redundant HAT activities.

claim: The NF-κB subunit RelA is acetylated on lysines 218, 221, and 310.
source: The NF-κB subunit RelA is acetylated on lysines 218, 221, and 310 and these modifications are required for full NF-κB activation (Chen et al., 2001; 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2001 and 2002.

claim: Acetylation of NF-κB RelA on lysines 218, 221, and 310 is required for full NF-κB activation.
source: The NF-κB subunit RelA is acetylated on lysines 218, 221, and 310 and these modifications are required for full NF-κB activation (Chen et al., 2001; 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2001 and 2002.

claim: Salicylate's NF-κB inhibitory effect can be at least partly explained by p300 inhibition.
source: Therefore, salicylate's NF-κB inhibitory effect can be at least partly explained by p300 inhibition.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that salicylate inhibits p300 and reduces NF-κB acetylation, which is required for NF-κB activation.

claim: AMPK inhibits p300 acetyltransferase activity by phosphorylating p300 at serine 89.
source: AMPK is reported to inhibit p300 acetyltransferase activity by phosphorylating p300 at serine 89 (Zhang et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2011.

claim: Many of the pleiotropic effects of salicylate on different cell types and in diseases, including leukemia, are mediated by specific inhibition of CBP/p300 acetyltransferase activity.
source: Overall, our findings suggest that many of the pleiotropic effects of salicylate on different cell types and in diseases, including leukemia, are mediated by specific inhibition of CBP/p300 acetyltransferase activity, leading to deacetylation of histones and non-histone proteins.
evidence: This is a broad conclusion inferred from the combined findings of the study.

claim: The IC50 for p300 inhibition by both salicylic acid and diflunisal was significantly lower in HEK293T cells than in HAT assays in vitro.
source: Interestingly, the IC50 for p300 inhibition by both salicylic acid and diflunisal was significantly lower in HEK293T cells (Figure 2A) than in HAT assays in vitro (Figure 1A).
evidence: Comparison of IC50 values from Figures 1A and 2A shows lower IC50 in cells (4.8 mM) than in vitro (10.2 mM for p300).

claim: AMPK activation in cells might enhance the p300 inhibitory effect of salicylate in cells.
source: First, AMPK activation in cells might enhance the p300 inhibitory effect of salicylate in cells (Zhang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the increased potency in cells, supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2011.

claim: Short-term treatment of cells with salicylate or diflunisal is associated with a decrease in the expression of p300.
source: Second, we have also observed that short-term treatment of cells with salicylate or diflunisal is associated with a decreased in the expression p300 (see Figure 2F and 3D).
evidence: Figures 2F and 3D show reduced p300 protein levels in cells treated with salicylate or diflunisal.

claim: The autoacetylation of p300 is important for its enzymatic activity.
source: and the autoacetylation of p300 is important for its enzymatic activity (Thompson et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Thompson et al., 2004.

claim: Inhibition of p300 autoacetylation could contribute to both the inactivation of the enzyme and a change in its stability.
source: While we have not further explored this interesting observation here, we could envisage a mechanism by which inhibition of p300 autoacetylation would both contribute to the inactivation of the enzyme but also to a change in its stability.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis to explain the observed decrease in p300 levels.

claim: Salicylate does not inhibit COX-1 and COX-2 activity in vitro.
source: However, salicylate does not, unlike its acetylated derivative aspirin, inhibit COX-1 and COX-2 activity in vitro (Vane, 1971) (Vargaftig, 1978; Mitchell et al., 1993); (Cromlish and Kennedy, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Vane, 1971; Vargaftig, 1978; Mitchell et al., 1993; and Cromlish and Kennedy, 1996.

claim: Salicylate has been shown to exert a comparable analgesic and anti-inflammatory action as aspirin.
source: However, salicylate has been shown to exert a comparable analgesic and anti-inflammatory action as aspirin.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about salicylate's pharmacological effects.

claim: Salicylate plasma concentrations in patients taking salicylic acid (3-4 g/day) range between 1-3 mM.
source: Further, it should also be noted that salicylate plasma concentrations in patients taking salicylic acid (3–4 g/day) range between 1–3 mM, a concentration at which partial inhibition of p300/CBP is observed.
evidence: This is stated as established pharmacokinetic information about salicylate.

claim: Partial or complete inhibition of p300 by salicylate represents one of its relevant biological targets.
source: These data are therefore consistent with the proposed model that partial or complete inhibition of p300 by salicylate represents one of its relevant biological targets.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the comparison of cellular IC50 values with plasma concentrations.

claim: The salicylate substructure is now identified in three HAT inhibitors, including anacardic acid, salicylic acid and diflunisal.
source: The salicylate substructure is now identified in three HAT inhibitors, including anacardic acid (6-nonadecyl salicylic acid) (Balasubramanyam et al., 2003), salicylic acid and diflunisal and might therefore represent an important scaffold for developing new p300 inhibitors.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings identifying the salicylate moiety as a common structural feature.

claim: The salicylate substructure might represent an important scaffold for developing new p300 inhibitors.
source: The salicylate substructure is now identified in three HAT inhibitors, including anacardic acid (6-nonadecyl salicylic acid) (Balasubramanyam et al., 2003), salicylic acid and diflunisal and might therefore represent an important scaffold for developing new p300 inhibitors.
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion based on the identification of salicylate as a common structural feature in p300 inhibitors.

claim: p300 has emerged as a potential therapeutic target for respiratory diseases, HIV infection, metabolic diseases, and cancer.
source: Recently, p300 has emerged as a potential therapeutic target for respiratory diseases, HIV infection, metabolic diseases, and cancer (Dekker and Haisma, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dekker and Haisma, 2009.

claim: Salicylate and diflunisal exhibit anti-tumor activity against a specific leukemia carrying a t(8;21) translocation.
source: Indeed, our findings show that salicylate and the related compound diflunisal exhibit anti-tumor activity against a specific leukemia carrying a t(8;21) translocation, a tumor previously reported to be dependent on p300 in vitro and in vivo (Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data in Figures 4 and 5, and citation to Wang et al., 2011.

claim: t(8;21) leukemia is dependent on p300 in vitro and in vivo.
source: Indeed, our findings show that salicylate and the related compound diflunisal exhibit anti-tumor activity against a specific leukemia carrying a t(8;21) translocation, a tumor previously reported to be dependent on p300 in vitro and in vivo (Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2011.

claim: Acetaminophen does not inhibit p300 acetyltransferase in vitro.
source: We have tested whether other NSAIDs, including acetaminophen and indomethacin, also inhibit p300 acetyltransferase in vitro, but did not detect any inhibitory activity (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation.

claim: Indomethacin does not inhibit p300 acetyltransferase in vitro.
source: We have tested whether other NSAIDs, including acetaminophen and indomethacin, also inhibit p300 acetyltransferase in vitro, but did not detect any inhibitory activity (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation.

claim: NSAIDs that lack p300 inhibitory activity failed to inhibit Kasumi-1 cell growth.
source: Importantly, NSAIDs that lack p300 inhibitory activity failed to inhibit Kasumi-1 cells growth (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation supporting the specificity of p300 inhibition for anti-leukemic effects.

claim: Salicylate and diflunisal identify a novel epigenetic therapeutic target, the epigenetic regulator CBP/p300.
source: These results identify a novel epigenetic therapeutic target for salicylate, the epigenetic regulator CBP/p300.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion of the study's findings.

claim: Salicylate may be useful for treating inflammation, diabetes, neurodegenerative disease, and other pathologies in which CBP/p300 has a critical role.
source: Our results also suggest that salicylate may be useful for treating inflammation, diabetes, neurodegenerative disease, and other pathologies in which CBP/p300 has a critical role.
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion based on the finding that salicylate inhibits CBP/p300.

claim: Diflunisal and salicylate have promise as an oral therapy for patients with acute myelogenous leukemia associated with a t(8;21) translocation.
source: Thus, diflunisal and salicylate have promise as a oral therapy for patients with acute myelogenous leukemia associated with a t(8;21) translocation, an exciting potential application of our observations..
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion based on the in vitro and in vivo anti-leukemic effects observed in the study.
